messages:
Maria: quick RFC follow-up — thinking about splitting continuous batching into two processes: ingest-collector (fast thin path, per-core) and dispatch-coordinator (global packing/eviction). thoughts on ownership, headroom signals, and cross-process handoff? we hit a p99 tail last week and want a clearer contract.

Alex: sounds promising. separation should reduce p99 jitter on fastpath. main worry is handoff overhead + extra indirection for queue slices.

Jamal: agree on p99 gains. kvcache affinity is tricky — if coordinator moves windows we need a warmup strategy that doesn't regress costs.

Sophie: could do pointer-only handoff: a small header packet stays mutable and payload lives in per-core slab. coordinator steals header referencing payload-id, avoids copy.

Maria: header shape proposal: tenant_id, token_estimate, deadline_hint, kvcache_tag, ownership_epoch. payload remains in slab with a payload_id.

Kai: ownership-transfer complexity: who frees slab? need explicit ownership tokens and a tiny state machine.

Jamal: sketch: states = PENDING -> OWNED_BY_COORDINATOR -> EXECUTING -> RELEASED. ownership_token is 64-bit; CAS flips token.

Alex: races: late-join requests during transfer. we should avoid silent acceptance; need backpressure or forwarding.

Maria: propose "soft-fence": when collector offers a window it's tagged SOFT_FENCED. collectors still accept late-joins but either (a) penalize (bump deadline), or (b) forward to coordinator for inclusion.

Sophie: API config example:
```
ingest.collector_threads = 12
ingest.soft_fence_timeout_ms = 10
dispatch.coordinator_threads = 2
dispatch.max_steals_per_cycle = 6
```
small explicit knobs.

Kai: telemetry needs: handoff_latency_ms, handoff_failures_total, payload_reference_bytes, header_cas_retries. detect stealing churn early.

Jamal: add kvcache_warmup_miss_count. frequent steals => warmup regressions.

Alex: central coordinator simplifies packing but is a bottleneck. consider hierarchical coordinators (per-socket local coordinator + occasional global rebalancer).

Maria: hierarchical looks good. local handles most steals; global for cross-socket imbalance.

Sophie: failure modes: coordinator crash mid-handoff. include header.epoch + reclaim_timeout; collectors can reclaim when epoch stale.

Kai: reclaim_timeout should be conservative (eg 3x median handoff_latency) to avoid double-warmups.

Jamal: also billing: ownership token should carry billing tags so costs follow the request even if moved.

Maria: agreed. billing_tag travels with ownership_token and stays immutable during EXECUTING.

Alex: implementation: avoid blocking syscalls on handoff. use lockfree ring + CAS on header; slowpath on CAS fail.

Sophie: CAS-only for common-case. fall back to RPC to coordinator on high contention.

Maria: action items:
- Jamal + Kai: define ownership token lifecycle, reclaim heuristics, billing propagation
- Alex + Sophie: prototype pointer-only header handoff with CAS, metrics
- Maria: write RFC sketch for hierarchical coordinators and edgecases

Kai: Q: preemptive eviction during handoff? coordinator should set eviction_flag; collector must support abort fastpath producing minimal error reply.

Maria: implement 200B fast abort reply path; coordinator attempts graceful drain but can force release.

Jamal: will add abort fastpath to collector API.

Alex: :thumbsup:

infra-bot: CI passed on branch pkt-handoff (build 4723)

Maria: will turn this into an RFC draft and ping for review later today.
